URL: https://relioclips.com/app
Title: Web app — Relio

# Make Shorts in your browser.
Relio runs in the browser: choose a video, let Relio AI suggest Shorts, edit captions and framing, and export MP4s. Nothing to install. Projects and videos are saved to your account and open on any device you sign in on.

**How does access work?**
Sign up at https://relioclips.com/signup. The Free plan includes 20 video minutes each month, 720p watermarked exports and 1 GB of cloud storage. Paid plans offer more minutes and watermark-free exports. See https://relioclips.com/pricing for details.

**Which browsers work?**
Current Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox on a computer.

**Which languages do captions support?**
Relio transcribes speech and writes captions in the language spoken in your video. Automatic filler-word cleanup currently works for English only.

URL: https://relioclips.com/faq
Title: Help & FAQs — Relio

A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS

# A little clarity. Then, create.
Everything to know before your first Short.

**How much does Relio cost?**
The Free plan includes 20 video minutes per month. Paid plans start at €9 per month for 150 video minutes; see https://relioclips.com/pricing for current details and local prices.

**What happens to my footage?**
Your source files, projects, preview, and rendering stay on your computer. Audio chunks, transcripts, sampled frames, and editor chat messages are sent for AI processing. On Mac, they go through Relio’s server and OpenRouter to an AI model; on Windows and Linux, they go to Google Gemini. Relio needs an internet connection; it has no offline AI mode.

**Can I change the Shorts Relio picks?**
Yes. Review and adjust every Short before export. Change the timing, choose Fill, Fit, or Split framing, try seven caption styles, or ask the editor chat to help with edits.

**Where can I post my exports?**
Relio exports vertical MP4 files: 720p on Free, or up to 4K on paid plans when your browser and computer support it. Upload them yourself to your favorite platforms. Direct publishing isn’t built in.

**Is this ready for my daily workflow?**
Relio is an early beta. The Mac pipeline works end to end, but you should review every clip and expect rough edges. Windows and Linux ports are available but still need verification on real devices. Read the current limits.

**Do I need a Relio account?**
On Mac, sign in to the app with your Relio account to use the AI service. Your dashboard also shows your export stats and history. Windows and Linux use your own Gemini API key instead. Create an account.

**How do I get started?**
Download Relio, sign in on Mac or add your Gemini API key on Windows or Linux, and import a video. See the three-step workflow for a quick tour.

### Something else on your mind?
Check the project documentation ↗ or share your feedback on GitHub ↗.

URL: https://relioclips.com/about
Title: About — Relio

ABOUT RELIO

# One video in. Many Shorts out.
Relio is a desktop app that turns long videos into vertical Shorts with captions.

### What Relio does
Import a podcast, lecture, interview or stream. Relio transcribes it, finds moments that stand on their own, and cuts them into vertical Shorts. It reframes each one for the small screen and adds captions in the language spoken in your video. You review every Short and make the final cut before you export.

### Who it’s for
Creators, podcasters and streamers who want more short-form videos from the long recordings they already make, without spending hours in an editor.

### Where it runs
Relio is an early beta for macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon. Windows and Linux ports have not yet been tested on real devices. Your source files and finished videos stay on your machine. See Privacy for what is sent for AI processing.

### Beta access
Sign in to try Relio during the beta. AI usage limits apply; check Settings in the app for your allowance. About beta access.

### Learn more
See features, how it works and the FAQs, or download Relio.

Title: Changelog — Relio

RELEASE NOTES

# Changelog
What's new in Relio Clips, newest first.

### 0.1
2026-11-06 · CURRENT

Relio Clips now runs in your browser at relioclips.com. Nothing to install.

#### New

- A new name: Prism is now Relio Clips, at relioclips.com.
- Make Shorts in the browser: upload a video, pick settings and captions, review the picks, and export MP4s.
- Your projects and videos follow your account to any computer (1 GB of cloud storage per account).
- Choose the language of the video, or leave it on Auto. Relio keeps one language for the whole video, sung lyrics included.
- How many Shorts and how long each one is start at Auto.
- A bigger video player in the editor.
- New sign-up and sign-in pages, with password reset.

#### Improved

- Relio AI no longer stops at busy times: it retries quietly and switches to a backup model when needed.
- Every Short that's ready is saved. If some couldn't be made, Relio says how many and offers Retry.
- Titles use words actually spoken in the clip.
- Vertical videos keep their whole frame.
- Settings › Usage shows which videos are only on this device, and why.
- Clearer error messages, without technical codes.

#### Fixed

- Pages taller than the window now scroll.
- Captions no longer leave gaps between phrases.
- Exporting works in Safari.

### 0.0.1
2026-10-26 · BETA

The first public beta, as desktop apps.

#### New

- Installers for macOS, Windows and Linux.
- A guided tutorial for your first video, with an optional editor tour. Replay it from Settings › Account.
- Sign in with a Relio account.

#### Fixed

- Email confirmation links open the Relio website.
- AI timeouts show an error instead of silently losing Shorts.
- Crops stay inside the frame for every video size.

### Early build
2026-10-18 – 10-20

- The first Relio editor for Mac: long video in, vertical Shorts out.
- AI picks the moments and frames the speaker.
- Caption styles and a timeline editor.

URL: https://relioclips.com/privacy
Title: Privacy — Relio

PRIVACY

# Your footage stays yours.
Plain-language summary of where your data goes. Last updated 2026-10-27.

### On your computer

- Your source video files. Relio copies them into a project and never changes the originals.

- Projects, previews and rendered MP4s.

### Sent for AI processing
Relio has no offline mode. On Mac, requests go through Relio’s server (Supabase) to OpenRouter; in the web app, through Relio’s server on Vercel and an AI model provider. Windows and Linux send requests directly to Google’s Gemini API using your own API key. The relevant providers’ terms apply to this data:

- Audio chunks of the part of the video you selected.

- Transcripts.

- Sampled frames for clip selection and subject tracking. Web final ranking may also send up to 12 stills from clips with little speech.

- Editor chat messages, with recent conversation and a short edit summary.
Temporary audio files are deleted after each request. The Mac server logs may include portions of model responses for diagnostics. See OpenRouter’s Privacy Policy and Terms, and Google’s Privacy Policy and Gemini API terms.

### Your Relio account
Your Relio account is stored with our database provider, Supabase. The account stores:

- Your email address and password. The password is stored hashed by Supabase Auth.

- Any Paddle subscription and customer IDs, status and next billing date, if associated with your account.

- One record per finished export from the Mac app: the date, number of Shorts, total length in seconds and export quality.

- One record per video you make Shorts from: a fingerprint of the file’s name and length (not the video), the day and its length in minutes.

- The total cost of your AI requests and any promo codes you redeemed, to enforce your allowance.
No video, audio, transcripts or titles are stored in your account. Database rules let each user read only their own records. Deleting your account deletes its export records.

### Questions or deletion requests
Open an issue on GitHub to ask a question or to have your account deleted.

This page describes how the software works. It is not legal advice.

Title: Terms — Relio

TERMS

# Terms of use
The short version: Relio is beta software, provided as is. Last updated 2026-10-27.

### The software
Relio is provided “as is”, without warranty of any kind.

### Beta status
Relio is early beta software. Review every Short before you publish it, and keep your own backups. The Windows and Linux versions have not been tested on real devices yet.

### Your content
You keep all rights to your videos and exports. You are responsible for having the rights to the footage you process and the Shorts you publish.

### AI processing
On Mac, Relio sends audio, transcripts and sampled frames through its server to OpenRouter, which passes them to an AI model provider. Windows and Linux send requests to Google’s Gemini API using your own API key. The relevant providers’ terms apply.

### Your account
Keep your password safe and don’t use the account to break the service or access other people’s data. Accounts may be removed if they are abused. See the Privacy page for what the account stores.

### Changes
These terms may change as Relio grows. The date at the top shows the latest version.

This is a plain-language draft, not legal advice.
